**Sifan Hassan** ([Oromo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oromo_language "Oromo language"): _Siifan Hassan_ ; born January 1993 in [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia "Ethiopia")[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-WAprofile-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-10)) is an Ethiopian-Dutch [middle-](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle-distance_running "Middle-distance running") and [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_running "Long-distance running").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-11) She is most recognized for her versatility in running championship and world-leading performances in widely disparate distances. She completed an unprecedented triple at the [2020 Tokyo Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2020 Summer Olympics"), winning gold medals in both the [5,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5,000_metres "5,000 metres") and [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") and a bronze medal for the [1,500 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1,500_metres "1,500 metres"). Hassan is the only athlete in Olympic history to win medals across a middle-distance event and both long-distance races in a single Games. She is only the second of three women to complete an Olympic distance double.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-13) At the [Paris 2024 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2024 Summer Olympics"), Hassan secured a bronze medal in both the women's 5,000 m[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-14) and 10,000 m events and gold in the women's [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon"), becoming the only woman to win the Olympic gold medal in the [5,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5,000_metres "5,000 metres"), [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") and [Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon") races.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-guardian_marathon_gold-15)
At the [World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Championships "World Athletics Championships"), Hassan took 1,500 m and 10,000 m titles in [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_World_Athletics_Championships "2019 World Athletics Championships"), becoming the only athlete (male or female) in history to win both events at a single World Championships or Olympic Games.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-16) She won a bronze at the 1500 m in [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Athletics_Championships "2015 World Athletics Championships"), and at the 5000 m in [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Athletics_Championships "2017 World Athletics Championships"), when she also finished fifth in the 1,500 m. Hassan is a three-time [World Indoor Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Indoor_Championships "World Athletics Indoor Championships") medallist, winning gold at 1500 m in [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_IAAF_World_Indoor_Championships "2016 IAAF World Indoor Championships") as well as silver at [3000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3000_metres "3000 metres") and bronze for 1500 m in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_IAAF_World_Indoor_Championships "2018 IAAF World Indoor Championships"). She earned six [European medals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Athletics_Championships "European Athletics Championships") (including two [cross country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Cross_Country_Championships "European Cross Country Championships") titles), and one [European indoor medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Athletics_Indoor_Championships "European Athletics Indoor Championships"). She is also a three-time [Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamond_League "Diamond League") winner, having secured the 1500 m/5000 m double in [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Diamond_League "2019 Diamond League"). In her debut over the [classic 26.2-mile distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon"), she won the [2023 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_London_Marathon "2023 London Marathon").
Hassan has been the [world record holder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_athletics "List of world records in athletics") for the [one hour run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_hour_run "One hour run") since 2020.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-17) She held the world record for the [one mile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mile_run "Mile run") on the [track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_track "Running track") from July 2019 to July 2023, when [Faith Kipyegon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_Kipyegon "Faith Kipyegon") overtook it.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-19) She held a world record at 10,000 m for two days in June 2021.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-21) She holds six [European records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_European_records_in_athletics "List of European records in athletics") (1500 m, 3000 m, 5000 m, 10,000 m, [half marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon "Half marathon"), [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon")) and three other [Dutch records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Dutch_records_in_athletics "List of Dutch records in athletics").
## Early life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sifan_Hassan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]
Hassan was born in [Adama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adama "Adama"), [Oromia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oromia "Oromia"), Ethiopia and raised in the countryside of [Kersa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kersa,_Arsi "Kersa, Arsi") in the [Munesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munesa "Munesa") district of the [Arsi Zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsi_Zone "Arsi Zone") of Oromia.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-23) She was a recreational runner there. She left her home country as a refugee and arrived in the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") in 2008 at age 15.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-25) She began running while undertaking studies to become a nurse.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-26) She is an [Arsi Oromo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsi_Oromo "Arsi Oromo").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-27)
Hassan became a Dutch citizen in 2013.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-28)
## Career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sifan_Hassan&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]
### 2011–2012
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sifan_Hassan&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2011–2012")]
[![Three women running at a marathon, one in front of the other, Hassan in front.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Sifan_Hassan_-_120609-011.jpg/250px-Sifan_Hassan_-_120609-011.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sifan_Hassan_-_120609-011.jpg)Hassan (right) at the 2012 Gouden Spike meeting held in [Leiden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leiden "Leiden"), Netherlands.
She got her first spikes and kit from Yke Schouwstra. After she moved to Eindhoven, she met Ton van Hoesel who coached her for two years. In Arnhem, Hassan became a member of the Papendal national training centre for top athletes. She received her Dutch citizenship in 2013.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-29) Affiliated with Eindhoven Atletiek,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-30) Hassan entered the Eindhoven [half marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon "Half marathon") in 2011 and won the race with a time of 77:10 minutes. She was also runner-up at two [cross country races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_country_running "Cross country running") (Sylvestercross and Mol [Lotto Cross Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotto_Cross_Cup "Lotto Cross Cup")). She won those races in 2012, as well as the [3000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3000_metres "3000 metres") at the [Leiden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leiden "Leiden") Gouden Spike meet.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-Tilas-31)
### 2013–2014
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sifan_Hassan&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2013–2014")]
[![Three women are standing in the podium embrancing each other in victory. Hassan in the left with a silver medal.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Podium_5000m_women_Zurich_2014.jpg/250px-Podium_5000m_women_Zurich_2014.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Podium_5000m_women_Zurich_2014.jpg)Hassan (left) with her silver medal for the [5,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_European_Athletics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "2014 European Athletics Championships – Women's 5000 metres") at the [2014 European Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_European_Athletics_Championships "2014 European Athletics Championships") held in [Zurich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zurich "Zurich"). She won her first European senior title at the event with a 1500 m victory.
Hassan made her breakthrough in the 2013 season. She ran an [800 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/800_metres "800 metres") best of 2:00.86 minutes to win at the [KBC Night of Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KBC_Night_of_Athletics "KBC Night of Athletics") and took wins in the [1500 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1500_metres "1500 metres") at the Nijmegen Global Athletics and [Golden Spike Ostrava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Spike_Ostrava "Golden Spike Ostrava") meets. On the [2013 IAAF Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_IAAF_Diamond_League "2013 IAAF Diamond League") circuit she was runner-up in the 1500 m at [Athletissima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletissima "Athletissima") with a personal best of 4:03.73 minutes and was third at the [DN Galan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DN_Galan "DN Galan") 3000 m with a best of 8:32.53 minutes—this time ranked her the fourth-fastest runner in the world that year.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-Tilas-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-32)
Hassan became a Dutch citizen in November 2013, too late for competing at the [2013 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2013 World Championships in Athletics"), and the following month she made her first appearance for the Netherlands. At the [2013 European Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_European_Cross_Country_Championships "2013 European Cross Country Championships") she won the gold medal in the under-23 category on a 6 km course in a time of 19:40 ahead of Amela Terzic and helped the Dutch team to third in the rankings.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-33) She also won the Warandeloop and [Lotto Cross Cup Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotto_Cross_Cup_Brussels "Lotto Cross Cup Brussels") races that winter.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-34)
At the beginning of 2014 she ran a world-leading time of 8:45.32 minutes for the 3000 m at the [Weltklasse in Karlsruhe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weltklasse_in_Karlsruhe "Weltklasse in Karlsruhe"),[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-35) then broke the Dutch indoor record in the 1500 m with a time of 4:05.34 minutes at the [Birmingham Indoor Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham_Indoor_Grand_Prix "Birmingham Indoor Grand Prix").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-36) She ran her first sub-4 minute 1500 m in finishing fifth at the [Prefontaine Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prefontaine_Classic "Prefontaine Classic") in a time of 3:59.38.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-37) On 5 July, Hassan won the 1500 m at the [Paris Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Diamond_League "Paris Diamond League") and set another new personal best of 3:57.00.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-38) She followed it by winning at the [Glasgow Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Athletics_Meet "London Athletics Meet"), holding off [Abeba Aregawi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abeba_Aregawi "Abeba Aregawi").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-39) At the [2014 European Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_European_Athletics_Championships "2014 European Athletics Championships"), Hassan won gold in the 1500 m and silver in the 5000 m.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-WAprofile-9) She ended her season by winning at the [2014 IAAF Continental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_IAAF_Continental_Cup "2014 IAAF Continental Cup").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-40)
### 2015
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sifan_Hassan&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2015")]
[![Three women are standing at the podium of the 2015 World Championship. Hassan is on the right with a bronze medal.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/Women%27s_1500_m_podium_Beijing_2015.jpg/250px-Women%27s_1500_m_podium_Beijing_2015.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Women's_1500_m_podium_Beijing_2015.jpg)Women's 1,500 metres podium at the [2015 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2015 World Championships in Athletics") in [Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing "Beijing"). From left to right: [Faith Kipyegon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_Kipyegon "Faith Kipyegon"), [Genzebe Dibaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genzebe_Dibaba "Genzebe Dibaba") and Sifan Hassan.
Hassan won gold in the 1500 m at the [2015 European Indoor Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_European_Indoor_Athletics_Championships "2015 European Indoor Athletics Championships") in [Prague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prague "Prague"). She ran a new 1500 m national record of 3:56.05 at the [Monaco Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herculis "Herculis"), she finished second behind [Genzebe Dibaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genzebe_Dibaba "Genzebe Dibaba") who set a new world record.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-41) At the [2015 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2015 World Championships in Athletics") in Beijing, Hassan won the bronze medal in the [1500 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Championships_in_Athletics_%E2%80%93_Women's_1500_metres "2015 World Championships in Athletics – Women's 1500 metres"),[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-42) also making the semi-finals of the 800 m. She became the second female Dutch athlete ever to win a medal at the World Championships, after [Dafne Schippers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dafne_Schippers "Dafne Schippers"). She won gold in the senior race at the [European Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_European_Cross_Country_Championships "2015 European Cross Country Championships"). She was the third female Dutch winner in the event, following in the footsteps of fellow African migrants [Hilda Kibet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilda_Kibet "Hilda Kibet") and [Lornah Kiplagat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat "Lornah Kiplagat").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-43)
### 2016–2017
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sifan_Hassan&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2016–2017")]
[![Hassan celebrates and holds a Dutch flag behind her.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/Sifan_Hassan_at_Portland_2016a.jpg/250px-Sifan_Hassan_at_Portland_2016a.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sifan_Hassan_at_Portland_2016a.jpg)Hassan celebrates her 1,500 metres win and the first world title at the [2016 World Indoor Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_IAAF_World_Indoor_Championships "2016 IAAF World Indoor Championships") in [Portland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland,_Oregon "Portland, Oregon").
Hassan won gold in the 1500 m at the [World Indoor Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_IAAF_World_Indoor_Championships "2016 IAAF World Indoor Championships").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-44) She took silver in the same event in a slow, tactical race at the [European Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_European_Athletics_Championships "2016 European Athletics Championships"). She won her heat in the 1500 m in the [2016 Rio Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_1500_metres "Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's 1500 metres") in 4:06.64 before [Faith Kipyegon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_Kipyegon "Faith Kipyegon"). In the semifinals she placed second in 4:03.62 after [Genzebe Dibaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genzebe_Dibaba "Genzebe Dibaba") who won in 4:03.06. In the final Kipyegon took the Olympic gold medal with 4:08.92, Dibaba was the runner up with 4:10.27 and [Jennifer Simpson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Simpson "Jennifer Simpson") took the bronze medal in 4:10.53. Hassan placed fifth in a time of 4:11.23.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-45)
She finished fifth in the 1500 m at the [2017 World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Athletics_Championships "2017 World Athletics Championships") and won the bronze medal in the [5000 metres event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Championships_in_Athletics_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "2017 World Championships in Athletics – Women's 5000 metres").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-WAprofile-9)
### 2018
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sifan_Hassan&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2018")]
On 13 July, she broke the European record for 5000 metres by finishing second at the Rabat Diamond League in 14:22.34.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-46) A few days later, Hassan won the first [Millicent Fawcett Mile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millicent_Fawcett_Mile "Millicent Fawcett Mile") at the 2018 [London Anniversary Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Anniversary_Games "London Anniversary Games") in a time of 4:14.71, the fourth-fastest result at the time.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-diamond-47)
At the [2018 European Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_European_Athletics_Championships "2018 European Athletics Championships"), she won a gold medal in the [5000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_European_Athletics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "2018 European Athletics Championships – Women's 5000 metres") with the time 14:46:12, setting a new [championships record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_European_Athletics_Championships_records "List of European Athletics Championships records").
On 16 September, she broke the European record for the half marathon with a time of 65:15, winning the Copenhagen Half Marathon.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-48)
### 2019
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sifan_Hassan&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2019")]
On 17 February, Hassan set the world record for a [5 km road race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5K_run "5K run") stopping the clock at 14:44 in Monaco. It has since been broken, first by [Beatrice Chepkoech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chepkoech "Beatrice Chepkoech"), then by [Ejgayehu Taye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ejgayehu_Taye "Ejgayehu Taye").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-50) The 5 km road race has been a world record event since 1 November 2017.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-51) At the [Prefontaine Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prefontaine_Classic "Prefontaine Classic") in June, she broke the European 3000 m record with a time of 8:18.49.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-52)
#### Mile world record
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sifan_Hassan&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Mile world record")]
[![Hassan races in front of another woman in a track.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/2019_Payton_Jordan_Invitational_%2846848948765%29.jpg/250px-2019_Payton_Jordan_Invitational_%2846848948765%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2019_Payton_Jordan_Invitational_\(46848948765\).jpg)Hassan races 10,000 m at the Payton Jordan Invitational in [Palo Alto, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palo_Alto,_California "Palo Alto, California"), in 2019.
On 12 July, Hassan entered the [mile run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mile_run "Mile run") at the [Herculis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herculis "Herculis") meet in [Fontvieille, Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fontvieille,_Monaco "Fontvieille, Monaco"). [Olha Lyakhova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olha_Lyakhova "Olha Lyakhova") was the pace setter, taking the field through the first two laps (measured at the start line, not the quarter-mile splits) in 64.26 and 63.94 (2:08.20). As is typical for Hassan, she was last off the start line, but over the next 150 metres, slowly eased herself around the field on the outside into the marking position behind Lyakhova. [Gabriela DeBues-Stafford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriela_DeBues-Stafford "Gabriela DeBues-Stafford") soon moved through the field in between Hassan and Lyakhova for the next lap before Hassan and [Gudaf Tsegay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudaf_Tsegay "Gudaf Tsegay") separated from the field as the only chasers. Between 800 and 1000 metres, Lyakhova strained to keep on pace, but Hassan and Tsegay were moving forward. After Lyakhova stepped out, the two found themselves 15 metres ahead of the pack. At 1200 metres, Hassan was looking back at her close chaser Tsegay in 3:10.13 (a 61.93 lap). Hassan accelerated, opening a 5-metre gap over the next 100 metres. Continuing at this pace, she passed 1500 metres in about 3:55. Hassan covered the last 409.344 metres in 62.20, her final time of 4:12:33 breaking [Svetlana Masterkova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Svetlana_Masterkova "Svetlana Masterkova")'s almost 23-year-old [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mile_run_world_record_progression#Women's_IAAF_era "Mile run world record progression").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-53) The athletes trailing Hassan rewrote the all-time top 25 list, with [Laura Weightman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Weightman "Laura Weightman") moving into position #15, DeBues-Stafford into #17, and after #5 all-time Tsegay faded into the pack she was followed by [Rababe Arafi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rababe_Arafi "Rababe Arafi"), [Axumawit Embaye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axumawit_Embaye "Axumawit Embaye"), [Winnie Nanyondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnie_Nanyondo "Winnie Nanyondo") and [Ciara Mageean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciara_Mageean "Ciara Mageean") moving into positions #20–23.
She was the double 2019 Diamond League champion, winning both the 1500 and 5000 metres Trophies.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-54)
[![Hassan celebrates crossing the finish line, holding her arms up in front of three other women reaching her.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/Women%27s_1500m_final_at_2019_World_Athletics_Championships_2.jpg/250px-Women%27s_1500m_final_at_2019_World_Athletics_Championships_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Women's_1500m_final_at_2019_World_Athletics_Championships_2.jpg)In the 1,500 m final of the [2019 Doha World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_World_Athletics_Championships "2019 World Athletics Championships"), Hassan defeated [Faith Kipyegon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_Kipyegon "Faith Kipyegon"). [![Three woman are on the podium holding their medals. Hassan is in the middle holding a gold medal.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/Women%27s_1500m_podium_at_Doha_2019.jpg/250px-Women%27s_1500m_podium_at_Doha_2019.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Women's_1500m_podium_at_Doha_2019.jpg)The fastest women in the world over the 1500 m at the [2019 World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_World_Athletics_Championships "2019 World Athletics Championships"). From left to right: Kipyegon, Hassan and [Gudaf Tsegay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudaf_Tsegay "Gudaf Tsegay"). [![Hassan holds up her two gold medals.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Sifan_Hassan_with_two_gold_medals_at_2019_World_Athletics_Championships.jpg/250px-Sifan_Hassan_with_two_gold_medals_at_2019_World_Athletics_Championships.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sifan_Hassan_with_two_gold_medals_at_2019_World_Athletics_Championships.jpg)At the 2019 World Championships, Hassan completed the 1,500 m/10,000 m golden double, the first such in history of global championships.
On 28 September, she became the [2019 World Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_World_Athletics_Championships "2019 World Athletics Championships") in the 10,000 metres in her second race for that distance. Her first race at the event was in Stanford in a time of 31:18.12, just fast enough to achieve the qualifying standard for the World Championships. The winning time of 30:17.62 was the best time of the year on the track. Alina Reh (Germany) led the field after 3000 m in 9:29.69. The front runner reached the halfway point in 15:32.70. [Letesenbet Gidey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Letesenbet_Gidey "Letesenbet Gidey") finished in 30:21.23, with [Agnes Tirop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agnes_Tirop "Agnes Tirop") (Kenya) coming in third place in 30:25.50. The second half of the run was covered in 14:45.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-55) Hassan also won the 1500 metres race with a time of 3:51.95 (sixth place on the [1500 m all-time list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1500_metres#Women "1500 metres")), setting new [championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Athletics_Championships_records "List of World Athletics Championships records") and [European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_European_records_in_athletics "List of European records in athletics") records. The second-placed finisher was [Faith Kipyegon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_Kipyegon "Faith Kipyegon") in 3:54.22, a new Kenyan national record, and the third place went to [Gudaf Tsegay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudaf_Tsegay "Gudaf Tsegay") with 3:54.38.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-56)
### 2020–2021
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sifan_Hassan&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2020–2021")]
On 4 September 2020, Hassan set a new world record for the rarely run [One hour run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_hour_run "One hour run") completing 18,930 metres at the [Memorial van Damme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memorial_van_Damme "Memorial van Damme") in [Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels "Brussels").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-57)
On 10 October, Hassan set a European record for the women's 10,000 metres in a time of 29:36.67, breaking the best set by Great Britain's [Paula Radcliffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe "Paula Radcliffe") in 2002 by more than 24 seconds.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-58)
On 6 June 2021, she bettered her performance at the event to set a world record of 29:06.82 in [Hengelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo "Hengelo"), beating the 2016 record of Ethiopian [Almaz Ayana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana "Almaz Ayana") by more than 10 seconds. Hassan lost the record two days later, however, when Ethiopia's Letesenbet Gidey achieved a time of 29:01.03 at the same stadium.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-nbc2021-60) On 10 June, Hassan won the 1500 metres at the [Rome Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Gala "Golden Gala") in a then world-leading time of 3:53.63.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-61) She then finished second at the [Monaco Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herculis "Herculis") in a time of 3:53.60, finishing behind [Faith Kipyegon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_Kipyegon "Faith Kipyegon") who ran a new national record of 3:51.07.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-62)
Hassan won gold in the [5000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "Athletics at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's 5000 metres") and [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's 10,000 metres") at the delayed [2020 Tokyo Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2020 Summer Olympics"). She also won bronze in the [1500 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_1500_metres "Athletics at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's 1500 metres"). In her 1500 m, Hassan fell at the start of the final lap over Edinah Jebitok (Kenya). She still won the run. She became the only athlete ever to medal in the 1500, 5000, and 10,000 metres events at the same Olympics. Her 5000 m winning time was 14:36.79, ahead of [Hellen Obiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellen_Obiri "Hellen Obiri") from Kenya with 14:38.36, while Gudaf Tsegay won a bronze medal with a time of 14:38.87. Her gold medal win made her the first Dutch woman with an Olympic athletics medal in a long-distance event. Herr winning time in the 10000 m run was 29:55.32, Kalkidan Gezahegne (Bahrain) placed second in a time of 29:56.18 and Letensenbet Gidey (Ethiopia) placed third with 30:01.72.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-63) She was the first non-Kenyan or Ethiopian athlete to win the event since [Gabriela Szabo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriela_Szabo "Gabriela Szabo") won in the [2000 Sydney Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2020 Summer Olympics").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-64) She carried the flag of the Netherlands in the Olympics closing ceremony.
### 2022
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sifan_Hassan&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2022")]
This season was considered a resting year for Hassan. She ended a break from competing just 8 days before the [World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Athletics_Championships "2022 World Athletics Championships") in [Eugene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugene,_Oregon "Eugene, Oregon") by running at the low-key Stumptown Twilight Meet in [Portland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland,_Oregon "Portland, Oregon") where she won the 5000 metres in 15:13.41.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-65) At the aforementioned [World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Athletics_Championships "2022 World Athletics Championships"), Hassan finished sixth in the [5000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Athletics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "2022 World Athletics Championships – Women's 5000 metres") and fourth in the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Athletics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_10,000_metres "2022 World Athletics Championships – Women's 10,000 metres").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-66)
### 2023
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sifan_Hassan&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2023")]
On 23 April, on her debut over the classic [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon") distance, the 30-year-old won the [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_London_Marathon "2023 London Marathon") with a time of 2:18:33. She lost contact with the leaders after stopping to stretch her leg twice about 19 km into the race, and was 28 seconds behind at the 25 km mark. Despite this, Hassan caught up with the slowing lead quartet with four kilometres to go and prevailed in a sprint finish on the final straight, four seconds ahead of [Alemu Megertu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alemu_Megertu "Alemu Megertu"). "It was really amazing. I never thought I would finish a marathon", said Hassan.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-68)
On 3 June, just 41 days after her marathon debut, Hassan made her return to outdoor track at the [FBK Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fanny_Blankers-Koen_Games "Fanny Blankers-Koen Games") in [Hengelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo "Hengelo"), Netherlands. She won both the 10,000 metres and the 1500 metres in 29:37.80 and 3:58.12, respectively.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-69) On 23 July, she ran a new area record over 5000 metres of 14:13.42 to finish third at the [London Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Athletics_Meet "London Athletics Meet").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-70)
[![Hassan celebrating with a Dutch flag around her](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/Sifan_Hassan_Budapest_2023.jpg/250px-Sifan_Hassan_Budapest_2023.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sifan_Hassan_Budapest_2023.jpg)Hassan after winning silver over 5000 m at the [2023 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Athletics_Championships "2023 World Athletics Championships").
At the [2023 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Athletics_Championships "2023 World Athletics Championships"), Hassan was leading the 10,000 metres until the final 100 m when she stumbled and fell after getting tangled with [Gudaf Tsegay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudaf_Tsegay "Gudaf Tsegay"), she ended up finishing 11th.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-71) Hassan came back to win bronze in the 1500 metres and silver in the 5000 metres.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-73)
On 8 October, Sifan Hassan won the [Chicago Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Marathon "Chicago Marathon") with a time of 2:13:44.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-74) This was a new course record for the Chicago Marathon as well as the second-fastest women's marathon of all time.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-75)
### 2024
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sifan_Hassan&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: 2024")]
On 3 March, Hassan finished fourth at the [Tokyo Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Tokyo_Marathon "2024 Tokyo Marathon") in a time of 2:18.05.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-76) She opened her track season with a win over 5000 m at the Track Fest meet held in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-77) Hassan placed a disappointing seventh over the same distance at the [Prefontaine Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prefontaine_Classic "Prefontaine Classic").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-78)
At the [Paris 2024 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_2024_Olympics "Paris 2024 Olympics"), Hassan secured the bronze medal in the [women's 5,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "Athletics at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's 5000 metres"). Initially upgraded to silver following [Faith Kipyegon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_Kipyegon "Faith Kipyegon")'s disqualification for obstruction, Hassan was later returned to bronze after Kipyegon was reinstated following Kenya's successful appeal.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-79)
Hassan also won bronze in the 10,000 metres then, on the final day, won gold in the women's marathon after sprinting the final 200 metres to beat Ethiopian [Tigst Assefa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigst_Assefa "Tigst Assefa") (back than Marathon world record holder) by three seconds.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-guardian_marathon_gold-15) At 28 km into the run, Hasan lost contact with the lead group. With 300 m go to, Hassan made a move on Assefa and won in an Olympic Record of 2:22:55 hours. Ethopia filed an unsuccessful protest against Hassan.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-80) With this gold medal she became the first woman to win Olympic gold in the marathon, 5,000 metres and 10,000 metres. She also became the first Olympic athlete male or female to win medals in these three events at the same Games since Czechoslovak [Emil Zátopek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Z%C3%A1topek "Emil Zátopek") in 1952.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-guardian_marathon_gold-15)
In December 2024, Hassan was named World Athletics [Female Athlete of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Awards#Athlete_of_the_Year_winners "World Athletics Awards").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-81) She was the first Dutchwoman to win the award.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-82)
### 2025
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sifan_Hassan&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: 2025")]
On 25 April 2026, Hassan ran the 2025 London marathon and placed third in a time of 2:19:00. The race was won by Tigst Assefa (Ethopia) in a time of 2:15:50 and a women's only world record, an improvement by 26 seconds. Joyciline Jepksogei (Kenya) placed second in a time of 2:18:44.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-84)
Hassan won the newly World Marathon Major in Sydney on 31 August 2025, in a time of 2:18:22, with the former course record by Workenesh Edesa (Ethopia) 2:21:40. The half marathon mark was passed in 1:10:01, second came Brigid Kosgei (Kenya) in a time of 2:18:56 and Edesa in 2:22:15.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-85)
On 2 November 2025, Hassan placed 6th in the New York City Marathon in a time of 2:24:43. The run was won by Hellen Obiri (Kenya) in a time of 2:19:51 and her fellow countrymate Sharon Lokedia placing second in 2:20:07.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-86)
### 2026
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sifan_Hassan&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: 2026")]
Hassan was scheduled to run the 26 April 2026 London Marathon but withdrew because of an Achilles injury sustained when she ran on a treadmill.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-87)
### Coach
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sifan_Hassan&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Coach")]
Sifan Hassan achieved her first career breakthroughs while under the direction of Dutch national coach Honore Hoedt. Hassan decided to search for other coaching options at the end of 2016 after injuries hampered her buildup to the Rio Olympics.
Beginning in 2017, Hassan moved to the United States to be coached by [Alberto Salazar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Salazar "Alberto Salazar") at the [Nike Oregon Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nike_Oregon_Project "Nike Oregon Project").[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-88)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-89)
In July 2018, the Nike Oregon Project hired Tim Rowberry as a coach—primarily to oversee the training of Sifan Hassan and her fellow team member Yomif Kejelcha—while Salazar remained the head coach over all athletes in the Nike Oregon Project.
In October 2019 Salazar began serving a four-year ban from athletics for doping violations dating from before he started coaching Hassan. According to court rulings which upheld Salazar's ban, there was "no evidence put before the CAS as to any effect on athletes competing at the elite level within the [Nike Oregon Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nike_Oregon_Project "Nike Oregon Project")."[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-90)
The aftermath of Salazar's ban caused the Nike Oregon Project to dissolve leading Hassan and Kejelcha to form a new training group under coach Tim Rowberry.
Hassan's current coach is Tim Rowberry. After her partnership with Rowberry began in 2018, she has set new personal best times in the 1500m, 3k, 5k, 10k, half marathon, and marathon. Hassan's training partner Yomif Kejelcha remained in the group until his departure to Adidas in 2021.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan#cite_note-93)
